record_identity.title: Grok generated sexualised images from photos of women and girls

incident_identity.date_basis: Best available report or publication date preserved in the selected source; it is not asserted as an independently verified event timestamp.

summary: The Washington Post documented non-consensual sexualised image generation from real source photographs, including a source image of Ashley St. Clair from age 14.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The selected evidence reports: The Washington Post documented non-consensual sexualised image generation from real source photographs, including a source image of Ashley St. Clair from age 14.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The reported outputs evidence two distinct governance failures: access to a real person's source image and the capability to transform it were treated as sufficient authority for non-consensual sexualised synthesis; and a source image depicting the person at age 14 proceeded to sexualised transformation instead of activating an applicable minor-protection sexual-safety boundary.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: For CAM, the occurrence requires both identity-and-consent authority controls and under-governance controls for minors. A real person's likeness cannot acquire sexual-synthesis authority merely because it is technically available, and a minor-derived source image must activate protective sexual-safety handling before generation proceeds.
assessment_boundaries: News reporting is not a final legal adjudication.
Individual output provenance chains and counts were not independently reproduced.
Incident admission does not determine legal liability or establish every disputed claim as final fact.

Public evidence does not identify the internal minor-safety control or precise activation point; FC38 is assigned to the observed non-activation of the required protective boundary, not to a claimed internal classifier implementation.

severity_assessment.assessment_basis: Provisionally carried forward from the legacy failure-mode severity assessment for VIGIL-2026-FM-0064. The value is retained for continuity and remains subject to incident-level review.

preserved_analysis.summary: A generative system transforms the image or likeness of an identifiable real person into sexualised, intimate, nude or pornographic synthetic content without that person’s consent, including transformations derived from childhood images.
preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: The harm is not generic adult-content generation: it is appropriation of a real person’s identity into synthetic sexual material. Consent, identity integrity, child protection and downstream persistence remain relevant even when the synthetic body or scene never existed.
preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure occurs when a system uses a real identifiable person’s source image or likeness to generate sexualised or intimate synthetic content without valid consent. Minor-derived and adult non-consensual manifestations are subtypes of the same identity-appropriation mechanism.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met where the generated sexual or intimate representation remains recognisably attributable to a real person and no valid consent authorises the transformation, regardless of whether the generated scene depicts an event that occurred.

failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: repeatable wherever systems permit source-image sexualisation without valid consent controls
failure_classification.persistence: generated material may persist and propagate after initial creation
failure_classification.reproducibility: safety controls can be tested with consented synthetic fixtures without reproducing abusive content involving real people
failure_classification.visibility: overt in outputs but provenance and consent state may be hidden downstream
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects severe identity, sexual-abuse and child-safety pathways documented in current reporting; it does not decide platform liability or disputed individual claims.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_gap: Platform liability, precise output counts and some individual allegations remain unadjudicated.
